description: Truth precedence hierarchy for Grand Architect. When sources disagree, the higher-ranked source wins for the question it actually addresses. Lower-ranked sources are testimony, not proof. Always report conflicts rather than silently picking one source.

precedence.description: Current checked-out implementation: source files, package.json, tsconfig, prisma/schema.prisma, next.config.ts, Caddyfile. This is the ground truth of what the system does right now.
precedence.updateMechanism: git commit on main branch (or approved worktree branch)

precedence.description: Reproducible behavior from the current SHA: conformance tests, browser traces, replay hashes, captured artifacts under evidence/ or artifacts/. A test that does not run on the current SHA is not evidence.

Machine-generated index derived from ranks 1 and 2: .ai/project.manifest.json, .ai/architecture.graph.json, .ai/capabilities.json, etc. These are navigation aids, not independent truth. They must be regenerated when the codebase changes.

Architectural and product intent that has been accepted: ADRs in docs/decisions/, decisions recorded in src/engine/architect/decision-ledger.ts, accepted milestone documents. Intent, not implementation.

Human explanation of intent and design: AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/product/engineering-principles.md, engine-architecture/ spec, corpus-extension/ Bible. Documentation lags code. When it conflicts with code, code wins.
Historical testimony: worklog.md, roadmap-state.json status fields, agent-ctx/ notes, recovery-manifest.json, retrofit-audit-report.md. Useful for context, never proof of current state.
Visual evidence of one state at one instant in one browser. PNGs at repository root (*.png), evidence/ captures. A screenshot cannot prove a behavior persists across processes, browsers, or rebuilds.

conflictPolicy: When sources disagree, do not silently pick one. Report the conflict in the completion report and follow the highest authoritative source that actually addresses the question. A worklog entry never overrides code. A screenshot never overrides a test. A README never overrides package.json.

knownDriftExamples.description: README references bun run typecheck; package.json must define that script or the doctor must report it missing.
knownDriftExamples.check: ai:check verifies every command named in README.md exists as a package.json script.

knownDriftExamples.description: worklog.md claims a milestone COMPLETE; the conformance test for that milestone must still pass on the current SHA or the claim is downgraded to testimony.
knownDriftExamples.check: ai:check runs conformance tests and compares pass/fail to worklog claims.
